einzeiler: The legendary 1962 prison break from Alcatraz and the enduring mystery of the escapees.
kurzfassung: Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers executed a meticulously planned escape from Alcatraz in June 1962 using handmade tools, dummy heads, and a raincoat raft. Despite official claims that the men drowned in the freezing bay waters, decades of subsequent sightings and family accounts suggest they may have survived. The prison's reputation for being inescapable led authorities to heavily downplay the possibility of success.
stichpunkte: Alcatraz originated as a Spanish pelican-inhabited island before being purchased by John C. Fremont and later fortified for the military.
The site evolved from a Civil War defense fortress and military prison into a high-security federal penitentiary in 1934.
Frank Morris, John Anglin, Clarence Anglin, and Alan West orchestrated a covert escape plan over a six-month period.
Inmates utilized sharpened spoons to slowly chip through concrete utility vent walls in their cells.
The escapees crafted lifelike dummy heads from paper mache, toothpaste, and human hair to deceive night guards during headcounts.
Using roughly 50 stolen raincoats and hot steam pipes, the men constructed a makeshift rubber raft and life preservers.
On June 11, 1962, three of the men successfully breached the utility corridor, climbed to the roof, and launched their raft into the bay.
Alan West was left behind in his cell because he failed to finish chipping through his wall in time.
While the FBI officially concluded the men drowned, numerous unverified sightings, anonymous letters, and family testimonies persist for decades.

kapitel.titel: The Aftermath and Mystery of Survival
History of Other Alcatraz Escape Attempts

clips.hook: The US government purchased Alcatraz for a fraction of today's value
clips.text: John C. Fremont acquired the island for five thousand dollars on behalf of the government, an amount that equals roughly two hundred sixteen thousand dollars today.

clips.hook: Dozens of prior escape attempts at Alcatraz
clips.text: Before the famous nineteen sixty-two breakout, twenty-nine separate attempts involving eighty individuals were recorded, with most prisoners either captured or consumed by the freezing bay currents.

clips.hook: Robbing a bank with a toy gun
clips.text: The Anglin brothers carried out a bank robbery using nothing more than a toy gun before eventually being captured by federal agents.

clips.hook: Crafting lifelike dummy heads with human hair
clips.text: The inmates fabricated convincing replica heads to place in their beds using a mixture of concrete dust, toothpaste, soap, toilet paper, and actual hair.

The federal penitentiary was forced to close its doors because operating a facility on a remote island required shipping in all essential supplies, making it far too expensive compared to mainland prisons.

beschreibung:
In San Francisco Bay sits the once mighty fortress, a place that held America's most dangerous criminals, a concrete prison built upon Devil's Island, surrounded by a tempestupus sea, fearsome winds and shark infested waters, a prison no man could escape... or so they claimed...
